newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks pare gains at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks pare gains at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks surrendered some gains at the close Friday as the market ran into technical resistance, dealers said.
"The market, which is aiming for 900, tested the intermediate target of 855, but gave back ground on a wave of selective profit-taking," said Jorge Bonanno at brokers Interfin.
The blue-chip MerVal index slipped off a high of 857 and closed at 850.62 with a gain of 0.6 percent.
It advanced 1.5 percent in the week to stand at a new five-year high and has risen 5.1 percent so far in July.

"The market is firm and stocks in sectors like construction and telecommunications will keep pushing higher," Bonanno said. "The tone is selective because investors are treading cautiously at these price levels."
Floor volume remained strong at 36.7 million pesos against 38 million Thursday, but over-the-counter turnover dwindled to just 61.9 million pesos from 139.5 million Thursday.

"Because of Wednesday's (Independence Day) holiday and because the tone has been somewhat volatile on Wall Street, some players are holding their bets. But liquidity remains very good," another dealer said.
The broad market closed up 0.3 percent, with winners beating losers 44 to 21 and 19 issues closing flat.
Strongest main-tier performers were foods giant Molinos and holding company Garovaglio, which both climbed 2.6 percent, and construction stock Polledo, up 1.9 percent.
MerVal losers were led by pulp and paper maker Celulosa, agricultural holding company Cresud and petrochemical concern Inudpa, which dropped 3.0 percent, 1.3 percent and 0.8 percent, respectively.
